# EnterpriseGlue v0.14.0 Release Notes

Generated from release-note fragments changed since `v0.13.1`.

## Highlights

- **product-neutral-plugin-platform:** Keeps the plugin installer container build aligned with the generated SDK, runtime, and installer package versions and streams lifecycle build evidence without a fixed child-process buffer.
- **product-neutral-plugin-platform:** Hardens plugin lifecycle and secret-broker file reads against time-of-check/time-of-use races and removes an inefficient plugin-ID validation expression before the v0.14.0 release.
- **product-neutral-plugin-platform:** Introduces the product-neutral OSS plugin platform, signed installer, isolated runtime, Carbon contribution surfaces, fine-grained host brokers, and lifecycle controls required by independently distributed plugins.
- **container-and-plugin-release-contracts:** Keeps source-built Docker environments aligned with the package-manager contract and makes published plugin host identity follow the immutable OSS release tag.

## User and administrator impact

- Plugin installer images can be built after an internal plugin package version changes without editing version-coupled archive filenames.
- Lifecycle qualification reports the complete Docker build output instead of masking an actionable packaging error behind a buffer failure.
- Plugin lifecycle state, receipts, plans, credentials, and broker policy files are verified and read through the same non-symlink file descriptor.
- Plugin installation and operation contracts remain compatible; no customer action is required beyond deploying the corrected v0.14.0 build.
- Administrators can install and operate compatible signed plugins without rebuilding EnterpriseGlue OSS or placing private plugin source in the public deployment.
- Authorized users see plugin workspaces inside their declared Mission Control parent and contextual actions only on engines, incidents, failed jobs, process instances, and batches they may read.
- Support-style plugins can present paged cases, questions, analysis, resolution choices, locally sanitized diagnostics, export, retention, deletion, stronger-model escalation, and human escalation through host-owned Carbon surfaces.
- Source-built EnterpriseGlue deployments no longer restart because a development Docker image installs a pnpm version that cannot read the committed lockfile.
- Published backends advertise their exact OSS release to the plugin compatibility resolver, so untested host and paid-plugin combinations remain blocked.

## Upgrade and compatibility

- Use @enterpriseglue/plugin-installer 0.1.2 or the matching v0.14.0 installer image when the plugin platform is released.
- Use the corrected v0.14.0 host and installer artifacts; do not publish or deploy the earlier unreleased candidate.
- Deploy the v0.14.0 OSS host before installing a plugin that declares host compatibility >=0.14.0 <0.15.0.
- Allow the normal TypeORM startup migration process to create the additive plugin tables and columns before enabling any plugin.
- Install plugins only from immutable signed OCI digests and use the v0.14.0 capability endpoint to verify exact SDK and shared-frontend compatibility.
- Rebuild source-based backend images so they use the corrected package-manager version.

## API and integration compatibility

- Adds versioned plugin manifest, resource, capability, distribution, control, contribution-availability, event, notification, schedule, storage, secret-use, and broker contracts.
- Adds authenticated plugin lifecycle, capability, asset, event-recovery, health, admission, and emergency-control APIs guarded by platform.settings.read or platform.settings.manage.
- Adds closed host brokers for safe identity, engine metadata, authorization-filtered engine access, local sanitized diagnostics, notifications, schedules, plugin-private storage, events, and indirect secret use.
- Adds host-owned desktop and responsive plugin navigation, route, settings, engine, incident, failed-job, process-instance, batch, and global-shell contribution points.

## Configuration

- Trusted plugin publishers, named egress policies, gateway limits, circuit-breaker settings, event retention, notification delivery, schedules, and local diagnostic sources remain deployment-owned host configuration.
- The installer must explicitly grant each host-broker permission; plugins cannot select another tenant, principal, engine, diagnostic path, credential, or egress destination.
- ION Support remains a separately distributed private plugin and is not included in the OSS image, repository, configuration defaults, or release artifact.

## Database migrations

- This packaging correction changes no database schema or stored plugin data.
- This hardening changes no database schema or stored plugin data.
- Migration: 1700000000114-add-plugin-platform.
- Migration: 1700000000115-add-plugin-broker-replay.
- Migration: 1700000000116-add-plugin-storage.

- Migration: 1700000000120-add-plugin-gateway-admission.
- Migration: 1700000000121-add-plugin-event-circuit.
- Migration: 1700000000122-add-plugin-contribution-availability.
- The migrations are additive and run after the v0.13.1 migration sequence on PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, SQL Server, Oracle, and Spanner adapters.
- Disabling, emergency-stopping, removing, or rolling the application back does not require destructive schema reversal.
- A full schema reversal can remove plugin lifecycle, delivery, schedule, storage, and availability data and therefore requires an approved export or database backup/restore plan.
- Database rollback supported for the combined release: no.

## Security

- The installer image still consumes only the three package archives produced in its isolated build stage and now asserts that exactly one archive exists for each package.
- Uses descriptor-based bounded reads with O_NOFOLLOW so file type, size, and content are evaluated without a check-then-open race.
- Replaces the ambiguous repeated plugin-ID regular expression with linear validation and explicit separator checks.
- Documents the secret broker's intentional credential sink only after tenant-bound signed policy, HTTPS, method, path, timeout, response-size, redirect, and reflection controls are enforced.
- Scopes missing-rate-limit suppressions to ephemeral loopback-only acceptance fixtures; production plugin routes remain protected by host gateway admission and rate limits.
- The host authenticates the caller, derives tenant and resource scope, enforces fine-grained access before rendering and execution, signs bounded gateway calls, and reauthorizes broker operations server-side.
- Plugin frontend assets are same-origin and integrity checked; plugin backend services are isolated behind the signed host gateway with explicit permissions, egress, rate, concurrency, and circuit-breaker policy.
- Raw customer logs, filesystem paths, credentials, signing keys, and unsanitized diagnostic bytes are not exposed to plugin frontend code or sent to a cloud agent; approved local collectors sanitize before signed handoff.
- The paid-plugin source and final-image boundary guards ensure private ION Support code, entitlements, prompts, cases, models, credentials, and customer data remain outside OSS artifacts.
- The patched npm and brace-expansion installation remains unchanged; only pnpm is aligned with the repository's declared package manager.

## Known limitations

- v0.14.0 supports the current SDK package and retains the previous SDK minor only where that package line and exact host evidence are present; compatibility is never inferred from a semver range alone.
- A plugin release is not supported until its private evidence is bound to the exact OSS commit, package versions, image digests, toolchain digests, and tested compatibility catalog.
- Plugin-specific customer cases, product governance, commercial entitlement, and human support workflows remain in the independently distributed plugin rather than the generic OSS administration plane.

## Rollback

- Revert the installer image and @enterpriseglue/plugin-installer package together; the earlier unreleased build requires manually aligned archive versions.
- Redeploying the merged plugin-platform candidate would reintroduce the reported CodeQL findings; roll back the complete unreleased candidate rather than selectively reverting this hardening.
- Disable or emergency-stop affected plugins first, then redeploy the previous OSS application image while preserving the additive plugin tables.
- Reinstall the previous signed plugin digest and matching runtime chart if the rollback includes a plugin release.
- Do not run destructive down migrations as part of routine rollback; export required plugin data or restore an approved database backup if complete schema removal is required.
- Restore the previous source Dockerfile and rebuild the image; production image contracts and persisted data are unaffected.
